findings.issue: “Image” is defensible, particularly in light of the carved images mentioned next, but ἵδρυμα can also designate a shrine or sacred establishment. This material alternative is not disclosed. This is lexical uncertainty, not evidence of source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining the contextual choice of “image” and preserving “shrine” or “sacred establishment” as alternatives. Alternatively, propose a different contextual rendering and submit it for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἱδρύσαντες γὰρ αὐτὰ μαγικαῖς τελεταῖς ἑορτὰς αὐτοῖς ὥρισαν
findings.english_quote: After installing the images with magical rites, they appointed festivals for them
findings.issue: The temporal rendering of the participle is defensible, but the explanatory γὰρ has no expressed counterpart. The source explicitly introduces an explanation of the Magi’s contrivance, rather than merely continuing the sequence of events.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: “For, after installing the images with magical rites, they appointed festivals for them”.

findings.source_quote: πολλῶν οὖν ἐν βίῳ παρελθουσῶν θρησκειῶν
findings.english_quote: Though many forms of worship have passed through the world
findings.issue: The genitive absolute can bear a contextual concessive interpretation, but “Though” does not represent the inferential οὖν. The draft replaces the source’s explicit inferential connection with a solely concessive opening.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: “Therefore, with many forms of worship having passed through the world,”. If retaining a concessive interpretation, still represent οὖν explicitly and explain that interpretation in the note.

findings.source_quote: πάρεσμεν φέροντες ὑμῖν (οἱ ἀγαθοὶ ἔμποροι) ἐκ προγόνων ἡμῖν παραδοθείσης καὶ φυλαχθείσης θρησκείας ὥσπερ μαργαρίτην
findings.english_quote: and a form of worship has been handed down to us from our ancestors and preserved, we—the good merchants—are here bringing it to you like a pearl
findings.issue: The clause concerning inherited and preserved worship has been moved ahead of the speakers’ presentation of it. Although the underlying interpretation is defensible and its grammatical alternative is disclosed, this reverses the supplied clause order.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the presentation first, followed by the inherited-worship description and pearl comparison. A candidate for fresh review is: “we—the good merchants—are here bringing you the form of worship handed down to us from our ancestors and preserved, like a pearl”. Retain the note explaining the genitive construction and its alternative interpretation.

findings.source_quote: ἐπὶ τῇ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος ἀπαλλαγῇ καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς εἰσαεὶ κολασθησομένας ἕξετε
findings.english_quote: upon release from the body you will also have your souls facing punishment forever
findings.issue: κολασθησομένας explicitly says that the souls will be punished. “Facing punishment” can describe exposure to, or anticipation of, punishment rather than its actual infliction, weakening the definite future-passive claim.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: “upon release from the body, you will also have your souls punished forever”, or “upon release from the body, your souls too will be punished forever”.

findings.source_quote: ἐνδομυχήσαντες γὰρ πολλῷ τῷ χρόνῳ καὶ τῇ ψυχῇ ἀνακίρνανται
findings.english_quote: After dwelling deep within for a long time, they become blended with the soul.
findings.issue: The explanatory γὰρ and additive καί are not represented. The source explains the preceding admission into the body and says that the demons also become blended with the soul.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: “For, after dwelling deep within for a long time, they also become blended with the soul.”

findings.source_quote: τῶν ἑαυτοῖς βοηθεῖν μὴ νοούντων ἢ καὶ μὴ βουλομένων
findings.english_quote: those who do not understand how to help themselves, or who are even unwilling
findings.issue: νοούντων governing βοηθεῖν naturally concerns thinking of or intending to help themselves. The draft introduces lack of knowledge about how to help, shifting the explanation of negligence toward practical ignorance. No note identifies or justifies that narrowing.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: “those who do not think to help themselves, or are even unwilling to do so”. Preserve “do not intend to help themselves” as a viable alternative if a note is supplied.
